properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/09/2024 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/03/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8210424
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2024
Comments: On 12/09/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1200 hours, weather was 40F and raining. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Stimulation activities for the two recently drilled wells are ongoing, equipment is located onsite to support these activities (photos #2-5). See inspection report #3878285 for more details. The accessible area excavated due to the release noted in inspection report #3878285 has been backfilled and fluids in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~701-741us/cm (photo #6). The remaining impacted area from this release will be excavated and backfilled upon removal of the rig matting covering that area. DEP Environmental Cleanups and Brownsfield personnel were onsite prior to my arrival to follow up on the release detailed in inspection report #3878285 and noted concerns regarding a diesel sheen observed on portions of the pad surface.The source of the diesel was investigated by Greylock and it was determined that a maintenance truck located onsite had released an undetermined amount of diesel, the truck was removed from the site and staff were working on removing diesel from the pad surface at the time of this inspection (photos #7-10). Fluid was observed overtopping from the secondary containment structure of the produced fluids offload area onsite (photos #11 and 12). This fluid was combining with rainwater and the diesel sheen on the pad surface and moving into the pad's drainage system which transports water from the pad surface to the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control. Fluids on the pad surface near the offload containment structure field measured for EC at ~10.32-15.93mS/cm; personnel from Penn E and R measured a similar result of 11.10mS/cm (photos #14-16).The pad drainage system services the site's infiltration basin via two pipes which move fluids from their respective half of the pad (photo #17). One pipe is located closer to the produced fluids offload area and the other is located near the wellheads. Fluid with a diesel sheen was observed discharging into the infiltration basin from the pipe near the offload area; this fluid field measured for EC at ~1.35mS/cm and the soil near this area field measured for EC at ~1.20mS/cm (photos #18-20). Fluid discharging from the pipe near the wellheads field measured for EC at ~0.908mS/cm (photo #21). Vacuum trucks were dispatched to remove fluids from the secondary containment structures and the pad surface in response to the release (photo #22). Personnel were also working to install sump pumps and shut in the drainage pipes to prevent any further discharge into the basin.I followed up with Greylock and they informed me that the drains discharging into the basin were shut in at 1400 hours and they were recovering fluids from basin with a vacuum truck.The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to prevent fluids from reaching PCSM controls until all contaminated fluids and soils are recovered.-Removing fluids from containment structures as it accumulates.-Following Act 2 to remediate the infiltration basin, diesel spill, and produced fluids containment release.Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #105-21962:-25 PA 78a64a(f) due to the observation of produced fluids overtopping from a secondary containment structure and being conveyed into the sites PCSM controls. -35 P.S. 691.401 due to the release of produced fluids and diesel discharging into the site's PCSM controls.The violations cited in inspection report #3878285 remain outstanding due to the remediation requirements outlined in 25 PA 78a.66(c)(2)(i) having not yet been met.I departed the site at 1345.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Cabot Oil &Amp; Gas Corp

Violation ID 669729
Permit API 115-21012
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Dimock Twp
Inspection Type Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date 2013-06-05
Comments 5/19//13 release occurred sometime between 8:00 PM and 9:00 PM. Cabot was fracing the E Woods 6H Well at the time. A problem occurred with the discharge pump on the blender. Crews decided to use a bypass on the tub. A problem occurred with a valve that isolated the tub. A reported 180 bbl overflowed the blender tub. It was reported that the fluid was freshwater with gel and biocide and potentially a gel breaker. Most of the release was contained; however 2 bbl escaped both the primary and secondary containment on site. Cabot’s reports stated that the berms caught the fluid but Somerset Regional Water Resources flushed freshwater down the grassy area adjacent to the pad and dug a sump for collection. Resource Environmental responded the following day and screened the area finding that there were no elevated conductivity readings and no hits above background on their PID. Violations associated with this inspection have been attached to the E Woods 6H Well (Permit #115-21012) 402- Potential pollution

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 959582
Permit API: 047-25102
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2022
Comments: This inspection is being performed in response to a report of a previous spill that occurred in February. It was reported that a containment overflow allowed production water to leak and eventually run down the access road and into a vegetated area, and was not reported to DEP. It appears as though the leak source is from a valve cluster sitting along the Billy Buck Rd. Some production water leaked and was cleaned up Feb 3. However, some of the product was not collected at the time and ran down the ditch/access road approximately 150 feet before crossing the access road and running into the pipeline corridor on the south side of Billy Buck Rd. The water appears to have spread across the corridor in multiple fingers, causing a kill zone in each location. Elevated conductivity readings >20 mS were noted on the pipeline corridor. The operator was contacted regarding these findings, and further investigation will be done to determine the scope and impact of the spill.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 908941
Permit API: 015-23612
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/25/2021
Comments: On 02/25/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) Tanner & Hana location. The drilling of 3 wells commenced on location between the dates of 11/12/2020 – 11/13/2020. Drilling operations subsequently followed, were documented within inspection report # 3127696, and had recently finished. The purpose of this inspection was to document the current status of the site and to inspect the site for any indication of possible releases of regulated substances. I arrived onsite at 1335 hours. At the time of my arrival, there were 3 semi-trucks that were hauling timber matting and what appeared to be plastic corrugated pipe off location. There were an additional 11 vehicles parked around the edge of the pad, but no crew members were identified. The weather was 44 degrees with mostly sunny skies. The pad surface was mostly covered in puddles, as warm temperatures melted snow / ice cover. The containment berm and slopes around the site still had approximately 4 – 6 inches of snow cover present. The 3 newly drilled wells were inspected, and all appeared to have back pressure valves set (photo # 3). There appeared to be a thick and dark fluid within each of the well cellars (photo # 4, 5). The area immediately surrounding the wells appeared to have been recently regraded with crushed stone (photo # 6). Just west of the wells, an oily odor was noted. There appeared to be a containment liner still present on the pad surface, partially buried (photo # 7). Puddles on the pad surface around this area (noted in photo # 15) all appeared to have an oily sheen and oily odor (photo # 9, 10, 11). Black specks were present within most of the puddles, and a concentration of a dark substance was noted within a puddle (photo # 12, 13). Sample # 9544-044 was collected from a puddle along the NW edge of the site where both an oily odor and sheen were noted (photo # 14). The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. The release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance to the pad surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a). Failure to report the release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance is in violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)1. Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23612. This release is referred to the DEP’s Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. The department recommends: 1. Dewatering the pad surface. 2. Dewatering the well cellars. 3. Removing the tarp liner noted in photo # 7 I departed the site at 1419 hours.

Inspection Date: 1/21/2026
Comments: On 1/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 18 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade and vegetated.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Toe preps were conducted last week to open the sleeves of each well. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Mark expects stimulation activities to start the first or second week of February, depending when the crew completes stimulation activities at a different pad. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected. I did witness a secondary containment measuring 6' x 6' with a valve connecting two pipes in it that had liquid in the containment that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The pipe connects the east production tank to one of the frac tanks on the west side of the pad. There was visible evidence of a release of material that overtopped the secondary containment structure. The release was observed in a frozen state, on the unprotected ground in an area measuring approximately 18" x 36" x 0.5" deep. I reported this to Mark who will contact production to have it cleaned.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1300 hours.

Violation ID: 8285396
Permit API: 019-22542
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Penn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on August 11, 2026 to report a release at the Bachelder Well Pad. It was hypothesized that one of the tank valves had failed, resulting in a leak that mixed with precipitation in the containment walls. The walls on the eastern edge of the containment then collapsed beneath the weight of the water, which overflowed onto the pad and ground outside of the pad. Ms. Breitenbach estimates that 110 barrels of fluid, some of which was rain water, escaped containment. Elevated conductivity was noted at several spots on and off of the pad, including beneath the containment liner and along the eastern grassy slope that led to the basin. At the time of the inspection, Moody and Associates, Inc. was on site to assess the extent of the release and assist with remediation. Excavation crews were present to begin removal of the contaminated materials.The problem has been contained and there do not appear to be any further threats to the surrounding site.

Comments: Weather: Warm, 80 degrees F, humid, no wind. I arrived to the location at 1110 on 6/24/2022. Brian Bowers (Company Man) accompanied me during the inspection. Seneca plans to stimulate a total of 7 gas wells (e.g. 1 Marcellus and 6 Utica) on the Cruttenden 846 pad over the next 2 months. Stimulation at the pad began on 6/17/2022. At the time of the inspection, Halliburton finished Stage 11 of 70 at the Cruttenden 31HU and Stage 16 of 80 at the Cruttenden 32HU; they are currently zipper fracing the Cruttenden 31HU and 32HU, which are both Utica wells. No abnormal pressures have been reported to date. Gas samples were collected from all 3 annuli at the Cruttenden 32HU at the conclusion of a pressure build-up test on 5/2/2022 (Inspection Record #3356904). Isotopic results confirmed the presence of combustible gas, primarily methane, at all 3 annuli. As a result, a violation of 78a.85(a)(5) was cited during an administrative inspection conducted on 5/26/2022 (Inspection Record #3368592); this is a continuing violation. No new violations were noted during this inspection. I left the location at 1145.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/22/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8188371
Permit API: 117-22214
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/23/2024
Comments: On 5/23/2024 at 0830 hrs., Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event Inspection (INCDT) of the Seneca Resources - Bauer 849 well pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. Complaint Id: 380888.I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello and Mark McCormick when I arrived at the site. Jeff explained the event as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between two wells, the 68HU and the 69HU. A BTI water hauling truck was offloading produced water into the frac tanks on the south side of the pad. When pressuring up, a pipe fitting on back site tube popped and sprayed out a mist of produced water. The estimated amount of water impacted a 20' x 50' area on the unprotect pad surface. Pictures 4 and 5 were supplied by Seneca personnel, showing the damaged pipe fitting. Pictures 7 and 8 were also supplied by Seneca personnel, showing the stained gravel surface. We viewed the area of the release. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was temporarily placed on secondary containment, awaiting the arrival of a rolloff dumpster. The crew was installing a secondary containment structure that will contain the rolloff dumpster when it arrives at the site. I field tested water puddles in various areas north of the frac tanks. An 8' x 6' water puddle between the utility trailers field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. 40' x 30' water puddle at the west end of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 2.19 mS conductance. A 35' x 40' water puddle on the unprotected pad surface about midway along the frac tanks field tested at 2.05 mS conductance. Puddles underneath the secondary containment structure that was being installed for the excavated material roll off dumpster field tested at 1.8 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field test at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit of tha Altairs PCTS5 is 19.99 mS conductance. Water in the east end of the offloading catch basin field tested and 18.03 mS conductance. Water in the west end field tested at 4.32 mS conductance. The crew was setting up to vacuum the water from the frac tank secondary containment ant the unloading catch basin. Mark said that he would have the crew suck up the fluid between the utility trailers.The site is stabilized with at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation. PCSM is addressed on site by a detention basin located on the south edge of location. It was adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. I did witness some temporary compost filter socks positioned around the location.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.2. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1045 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BURNETT OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/10/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8241239
Permit API: 129-28648
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Fairfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/10/2025
Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following an Oil and Gas Inspector referral during IR 4010435 where the Department observed the following:"There are two areas that appear to have oil staining. The area Southeast of the well is where the pump was during plugging and is approximately 25feet long and extends under the frac tank. The area North of the plugged well has several smaller spots 1-3 feet in diameter, and is where the rig was placed during plugging."Accompanying during today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations for the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are being issued under 129-28411.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Stickle well site to have 2 wells on it. The 1H: 129- 28411 well appears to be in production, while the 1H: 129-28648 appeared to be plugged with a vented monument. A well marker was observed to be leaning up against the wellhead with the well's permit number and a plug date of 7/17/2018, however, according to Department inspection records, this well was reportedly re-plugged on 7/1/2025. The Department is requesting Oil and Gas Inspector follow-up for evaluation of compliance for the well marker. The Department did not observe any active fluid leaks or fluid discharges coming from or near this reportedly re-plugged well. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the two frac tanks, the half round flow back tank and the trailer that were observed during IR 4010435 to be removed from the well site. The 25' long oil stain where the frac tanks were, along with multiple oil stained spots where the rig was sitting were observed on the graveled well pad. The oily substance did not have a sheen but had an unrecognizable odor. The Department screened the oil stained areas with a conductivity meter and collected readings of 0.1422 mS, 0.215 mS, and 0.0019 mS. The Department also observed darker soil around the plugged well, therefore this area was screened as well and a reading of 0.0343 mS was collected. The Department also observed a metallic gold thick substance on the gravel in one of the oil stains, this substance appears to be pipe sealant. The Department recommends the Operator remediate these release(s) in accordance with 78a66(c)(1).The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and a plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is also requesting the Operator clarify what the oily substance(s) is, how the release was quantified and submit the waste manifest from the site remediation upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the oily substance(s) on the graveled well pad.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 988204
Permit API: 081-21298
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/15/2023
Comments: On March 15, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection (CTS No. 370596) at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad G. Kirby Steck with Range Resources reported a spill of about 15-20 gallons of produced fluid from a rolloff dumpster located on the pad from a recent clean out service of the 9H Well on March 14, 2023. There was some residual produced fluid remaining in the containment from the clean out equipment that was placed in the dumpster and overwhelmed the secondary containment the dumpster was located in. The produced fluid was spilled on the well pad surface. Range Resources began removing the impacted soil on the evening of March 14, 2023. Range Resources excavated the top surface of the well pad of an area of about 40 ft. x 30 ft. The DEP attempted to screen the area of excavation with a soil conductivity meter but the ground was too frozen to acquire a reading. Mr. Steck said that Range Resources needs to remove a small amount of impacted soil next to the roll off dumpster but the equipment onsite was not able to complete the excavation. Equipment small enough to finish the excavation is planned to arrive on March 15, 2023.DEP spoke with Mr. Steck around 1300 on March 15, 2023 and he said the additional rolloff dumpster arrived. Range Resources was able to finish the excavation and add the impacted soil into the dumpster. Containment for this rolloff dumpster was in route to the site.The spill of produced fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Stream Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The violations noted have been immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/11/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Cumberland Twp, Greene county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 981469
Permit API: 059-23697
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/11/2023
Comments: On 1/11/23 a follow-up inspection of the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/24/22 (IR: 3445085) and outstanding violations issued on 11/23/22 (IR: 3462090).Background:On 10/24/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well Site (IR: 3445085). Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. An operator response was received by the Department on 11/8/22 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, and a new tank had been installed. On 11/23/22 a follow-up inspection was conducted and elevated conductivity was still observed in soil inside of the containment berm for the production tank (IR: 3462090). Outstanding violations were issued.Findings:-The area that exhibited elevated conductivity due to a leak in the corroded tank appeared to have been remediated. No elevated conductivity readings were obtained in that area of the containment (Photo #1). -The new tank was not hooked up to the well. -The pipe that had previously been attached to the old tank was not capped off (Photo #2), and a slow drip of fluid was observed coming from the pipe and hitting the ground below.-The substrate that was below the leaking pipe was stained and exhibited elevated conductivity (Photos #3-4).I informed Bryan Goletz of Diversified of my findings. According to Diversified in the NOV response dated 11/8/22 related to the first violations issued on 10/24/22, "The tank was not in service at the time of the inspection and the well doesn't produce fluid when in production". However, the fluid in the old tank during the initial inspection was at least shoulder height. And fluid is slowly, yet actively dripping from the pipe that should terminate at the tank. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a) and 78.54 are being issued.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions at the Taft 851 well pad. Meeting on site with Seneca Company Man Carlos Martinez. Weather conditions are mostly sunny and 65F.According to Mr. Martinez, the Patterson 805 rig is tripping drill pipe back into the well following a tool change. The rig is working on the tangent section of the 71HU well (API# 117-22261). The rig will resume drilling at a depth of 8,786' and work to a Total Depth of 24,073'. Drilling will resume around 1600 hours. This is the fourth well of eight total to be drilled in this setup. There are five wells in production at this well pad. Solids control in the rig backyard is managed by White's Energy Services. Shakers and centrifuges are idle at time of inspection. Steel bins are mostly empty of drill cuttings. The rig mats in the backyard are clean and free of debris (photos 3-6). Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form A application for the Taft Pad on 4/25/25. The Department approved the request on 5/1/25. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.During this inspection, water along the north pad ditch line was screened for elevated conductivity using an Oakton PCTS50 meter. Water with electrical conductivity (4.02 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 12). Water within the sediment basin was screened and found to have elevated conductivity reading of 2.29 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.The Department requests Seneca submit copies of weekly containment inspection and repair logs for the dates August 4-August 25, to juabbott@pa.gov.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Violation ID: 997048
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/31/2023
Comments: Site inspection conducted at the COP Tract 551B pad to review use of EWS VOX4 evaporators for processing flowback water. Meeting on site today with EWS representative Pat Pascarella. There are no EQT personnel on site at time of inspection. A TetraTek crew is loading produced fluid into water trucks. Weather conditions are partly sunny and 73 degrees F. Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Evaporators process fluid in batches, with automated systems in use to pump water into the system from the production fluid tanks and out to the frac tank batteries when fluid is concentrated. All pipelines and fluid control systems appear to be functioning as designed and there is no fluid or precipitation within evaporator containment. As authorized under the Air Quality Request for Determination Operating Permit, EQT will take four evaporators out of service after the initial 60 days of use. According to Mr. Pascarella, four units will be disconnected on June 13. There are no violations associated with the evaporator authorization. Fluid with elevated conductivity (3.14 mS/cm) is still present at the NE pad sump (photo 7). Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 25.13 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 0.37 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 98.26 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for broken and corroded piping and a release from broken and corroded piping.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4106039, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department attempted to contact the Operator by calling the number posted on the well tag, however, the number was not in service, therefore violations are being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate information posted on the well posting.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank under/adjacent to the corroded pipes. Although, these soil conductivity readings (0.0328 mS, 0.0899 mS, and 0.0244 mS) are not elevated, it does not visual appear that the release that previously occurred has yet to be remediated as vegetation in this area appears to be distressed and the gravel in this area is stained. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping is to remain outstanding at this time and new violations are being issued at this time for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.

Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. The EC of the fluid present in the trench along the southeast edge of the well head secondary containment was between 4.03 mS/cm and 5.06 mS/cm. The 30 ft by 50 ft area of the pad surface reported to have been impacted by the release southeast of the well heads had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 2.48 mS/cm and 4.00 mS/cm. A vaccum truck was sucking up fluid from the impacted area of the pad surface during this inspection. Other areas of the pad surface had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 856 uS/cm to 1990 uS/cm. According to the company man, excavation of this area was going to be completed by Tobias Machining, present on site during this inspection, and characterization of the site would be conducted by Penn E and R who was en-route to the site during this inspection. The Department requests a justification for the estimated release volume. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up fluid with elevated EC from the pad surface. Violations noted against permit 081-21945 for the 6/6/24 reported release. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the 5/8/24 release discovered by the Department. These violations will be closed upon attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-015 collected on 8/10/2022 at 14:00 as part of inspection report #3405181 at the Repsol Johnson (02-135) Well Site. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-015 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Barium - 122 ug/L; Strontium- 7.21 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- 4,900 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 904.1 mg/L. (Photo 1)Repsol submitted a 15 day response to NOV #406500 on August 30, 2022. According to the response letter, Resource Environmental was engaged to conduct site characterization work for an unknown volume of 'suspected produced water' spilled to the stormwater, soils, and gravels of the Johnson Pad. On August 11, 2022, Resource Environmental conducted screening surveys of stormwater pools and measured Electrical Conductivity readings of between 1.61 and 7.14 mS/cm on the pad surface. Additional characterization took place on August 12, 2022 through the collection of soil samples. Resource Environmental will conduct followup screenings and further site delineation is scheduled for September 6, 2022 following the removal of mobile tanks from the impacted area. Violations noted.

Inspection Date: 3/22/2023
Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Mac Well Pad site was conducted in response to a report of a spill that was reported to the Department on 3/21/23. Background:On 3/21/23 I received a call from DJ Hardy of EQT. He informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department's telephone hotline. The spill had occurred on the Mac Well pad when flowback was being conducted. EQT was investigating the cause of the spill but it appeared that the flowback had resulted in sand settling in the first tank in the series. The sand had caused the level of fluid in the first tank to fill faster than the subsequent tanks. The level rose and was released out of a valve at the top of the tank. The produced fluid misted out of the valve into the secondary containment, onto the gravel pad, and onto the northwestern vegetated slope of the well pad. SPSI had been contracted for remediation. Mr. Hardy stated he estimated that approximately 20 gallons of brine were released. I scheduled a field meeting with Mr. Hardy for the next day (3/22/23).During the inspection the following was observed:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-Some residual sand was observed on the side of the tank that had overflowed, and some impacted fluid was observed in the secondary containment (Photos #1-4).-The secondary containment appeared to be structurally sound, and no evidence of leaks were detected (Photos #5-8).-Substrate appeared to have been excavated from the spill area and fresh gravel was observed (Photos #8-10).-Vegetation had been removed from the northwestern pad slope (Photos #11-12). According to Mr. Hardy, the production fluid misted the vegetation but did not appear to saturated the soil below the vegetation.-Two roll-off containers were present on the pad (Photo #13). Mr. Hardy stated that only one container was needed for the waste.-No elevated conductivity was observed in the spill area, immediately outside of the spill area, on the pad berm, or on the vegetated pad slope (Photos #15-18).According to Mr. Hardy, the spill outside of the containment has been remediated. EQT plans to clean the tanks, flush, and vacuum out the secondary containment to dispose of any impacted fluid.Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 78a54 are being noted as immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Howard Drilling Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-24
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 875274
Permit API: 063-32818
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Conemaugh Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both pads and the access road following multiple violations on Pad B for releases and the access road for sediment discharges into the waters of the commonwealth. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet accompanied me on this inspection. Along the access road, two new lines of compost filter sock have been installed at UNT 18 to Frozen Run. The stream crossing appears to be in good condition. On Pad B, the modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) has been removed from the pad. Some excavation appears to have taken place in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS had been. The electrical conductivity of the fluid on the pad ranged from 1641 uS/cm to 2780 uS/cm in the northeast corner of the pad. A portion of the north stormwater channel has been excavated in the northcentral area of the pad. The excavated trenches in the northcentral area of the pad remain. Construction on the underground flow lines and the production equipment was on-going during this inspection. Two trenches were present along the well heads. Violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP for the sediment discharges along the access road into the waters of the commonwealth.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.
